title: Every v15.1 scene gains step uids and zero ids, so links and saved scenes get longer
detail: Constr.syncSteps runs on every load and every chain change (app.js cmLoad and cmChain). It gives every step a uid 'f<n>' and every zeros-and-poles step zpIds, and it takes those ids from state.nextId. Both fields are saved: in localStorage, in the link payload (figureState -> Params.encodeLink), in scene files and in sceneMeta. This happens even when nothing in the scene is a construction. v15.1 links still open the same, but the same scene now encodes to a longer link and saves different bytes. Large figures come closer to Params.LINK_WARN and LINK_MAX.
evidence: test/rgr_cdp/c_links.js: links made by v15.1 from examples 2, 5, 9 and 12, re-encoded by v16 after opening: 637->648, 649->660, 636->690, 684->744 characters (+2% to +9%). The state opened from the link and from the saved scene was the same in v15.1 and v16 (shapes, targets, params, steps), and the canvases matched (0.000% of pixels differ by more than 8).
fix: Save uid and zpIds only when a shape refers to that step or zero; strip them in noRuntime/figureState otherwise. Or keep them as runtime fields (_uid) and write them only when referenced. Leave nextId alone until a ref needs an id.

title: Plain huge circles and discs (not constructions) now use the new M(R) sampling
detail: region.js curvesOf calls bigCircle(s, win) for every circle and disc. Through Region.formOf -> Constr.formOfFields, a plain v15 circle or disc whose radius is more than 50 times the window diagonal now uses mrCurve/Constr.sampleMR instead of v15.1's sampling. The images may well be better, but this changes rendering and cost of existing v15.1 scenes outside constructions (deep zoom-ins on a circle; export of such a view). No paired timing or golden covers it, unless the quality suite's far-disc scene happens to reach r > 50 x diag.
evidence: Diff of src/region.js against notes/v15.1-candidate/src/region.js (+bigCircle, MR_RATIO = 50, `if (big) return [big]` in curvesOf). The quality suite still passes (81 runs, 0 failed), so nothing it covers got worse.
fix: Either limit bigCircle to shapes with s._g (constructions) for v16, or add a quality scene (and a perf pair) with a plain unit circle seen through a window 1e-3 wide, in X and through 1/z, and record it as NEW.

title: The new shape GLSL in gl.js has no GPU-vs-CPU check; the GLSL test results do not cover it
detail: v16 adds shader branches in gl.js: areaLevel kind 8 (gdisc), curveNear kind 20 (gcurve: two Newton steps), ixKindLevel 8 with its Lambda rule, and ixClipPiece type 4 ('g'). glsl-test and glsl-test-adv only inline cx/parse/funcs/glsl.js, which did not change. Their pages are byte-identical to v15.1's, so 'glsl-test 0, glsl-test-adv 304' holds by construction and says nothing about the new code. glsl_inverse_cmd.js (the inverse-renderer parity test, the right home for these branches) was run neither by CORE (AS-BUILT-core 'Not done' 2) nor by INTERFACE. I did not run it either: it can take up to 30 minutes.
evidence: Rebuilt glsl-test.html and glsl-test-adv.html from work/xvc sources: sha256 96129e6c... and 71ba6c14..., identical to notes/v15.1-candidate/evidence/glsl_pages.sha256. No test file references gdisc, gcurve or setFormAnchor.
fix: Add gdisc/gcurve rows (with a far anchor and a complement) to glsl_inverse_test.js's clip and walk sections. Run glsl_inverse_cmd.js on v16 and on v15.1 before the merge into v15.2.

title: Drawing tools and handle drags now run the snap search over all shapes on every pointer move
detail: Construct.hover (drawing tools and Point, Snap on by default) and Construct.handleMove (every handle drag in Select) call snapAt. snapAt walks every shape's handles, then calls piecesOf for every shape; piecesOf keys its cache with JSON.stringify(s) on each call, then does pairwise meetNear for the pieces near the pointer. v15.1 did only snapZ (the grid). This is cheap at 40 simple shapes, but its cost grows with the number of shapes and with long point lists (freehand, lasso, polygons with many vertices), because each one is stringified on every move. The handle-drag case was not measured: in my run the press did not grab the radius handle in either build.
evidence: Paired v16/v15.1, same session, interleaved, 40 shapes, Disc tool hover and draw: pointermove p95 0.4 and 0.5 ms (v16) vs 0.2 and 0.3 ms (v15.1); rAF work p95 0.1 ms in both; frame p95 16.7-16.8 ms in both (BUDGET60 met). Code: construct.js piecesOf (JSON.stringify key), snapAt, handleMove; app.js onMove 'handle' and hover hooks.
fix: Key the piece cache on a cheap per-shape version (bumped in shapesChanged or setHandle) instead of JSON.stringify. Prefilter shapes by a cached screen bbox around the pointer before pieceDist. Add a paired timing for a handle drag among 100 shapes, including a 2000-point freehand shape.

title: v15 gestures that now behave differently (as the spec intends): worth a line in What's new
detail: (a) With a drawing tool, a press on a zero or pole of f1 now starts a shape bound to it; in v15.1 it dragged the zero (app.js onDown: zpHit only in Select and Point [C1]). (b) The Point tool within 6 px of a stroke now makes a point that slides on the curve, not a free point (Alt places freely). (c) A handle drag in Select now snaps to points and crossings within 8 px and binds on release; v15.1 snapped to the grid only. The acceptance files pass, so none of them pinned the old behaviour, but returning users will notice.
evidence: Diff of src/app.js against v15.1 (onDown zpHit condition; editDown Construct.pointDown; onMove 'handle' -> Construct.handleMove; onUp Construct.handleUp). construct.js classesFor('select', 'handle') = points + crossings.
fix: No code change needed. Name (a)-(c) in the release notes and the tour's Constructions chapter (the Alt escape hatch especially).

title: t_sphere.js failed once under load and passed on the rerun
detail: One run of test/t_sphere.js, made while the quality suite's Chrome was running (load average about 23), ended '1 FAILED'. The immediate rerun ended 'all passed'. sphere.js did not change in v16, so this is a flaky timing or budget check under load, not a v16 regression. I did not check it against v15.1 under the same load.
evidence: First node sweep: 't_sphere.js 39s :: ... 1 FAILED'; rerun: '... all passed'.
fix: None for v16. Gates should run node tests apart from browser suites.
